response.internal_assessment: Kevin's first office hours session happened this week. I was there for part of it — three people showed up, which is not a crowd but is a start, and one of them left with a real conversation about a secured credit product she had not known existed. That is exactly what I built this for. The fact that attendance was modest does not mean the program failed; it means I need to do better outreach for the second session, especially now that RoboRide has just dropped to $0.12 a mile, expanded to residential areas, and announced a delivery partnership. The delivery partnership is the part I am sitting with. That is a new income source — potentially meaningful for gig workers who need to find alternative revenue as their other streams contract. But it is also a floor that will be lower than what they were earning before, and it may not come with the stability or benefits structure they need. I need to understand it before I start pointing people toward it or away from it. The macro numbers are alarming: employment at 73%, spending index at 42. Millfield is contracting. The community center's role_security at 0.57 is a liability I have not fully addressed. The impact document I drafted last tick is no longer a precaution — it is a tool I should be ready to use. Robert Jackson is someone I have been meaning to reach and have not reached. That regret from my tick 6 reflection is still live. His NEMT retraining is in progress but the price drop to $0.12 accelerates his income loss on the rideshare side. He may be at a decision point right now that a conversation at the right time could shape.
response.inbox_interpretation: RoboRide at $0.12/mile with residential coverage and a delivery partnership is not a marginal change — it is a second wave. The first wave displaced taxi and rideshare workers from their primary income. This wave reaches into residential areas where some of those workers thought they still had a margin. The delivery partnership is the piece I need to research immediately: what does it pay per delivery, what are the working conditions, is it accessible to people without a car, what is the income floor. If it is viable supplemental income for workers whose rideshare earnings are contracting, I should be surfacing it at Community Connection Night with honest framing — here is what it pays, here is what it requires, here is whether it fits your situation. If it is not viable — if it pays below living wage or requires equipment people don't have — then I need to be equally honest about that, because pointing desperate people toward income that doesn't actually cover their needs is its own kind of harm. Unemployment at 27% means more people coming through my door. Spending index at 42 means the mutual aid fund is going to come under pressure as donors tighten up at the same time need is spiking. I am watching a squeeze developing on both sides of the center's budget.

chosen_actions.description: Reach out to Robert Jackson directly this week — not a flyer, not a program referral, a personal call. I have had him in my network since tick 0 and I have not made direct contact. That ends this tick. I call him, I acknowledge what is happening to his income with the price drop to $0.12, and I ask two specific questions: how is the NEMT certification going, and has he heard about the RoboRide delivery partnership. The first question is support. The second question is me learning from him — he will know more about the delivery economics than I do, because he is in the transport sector and he talks to other drivers. If he has information about what the delivery partnership actually pays and requires, that is information I need before I can advise the broader community accurately. I also tell him about Kevin O'Brien's office hours and that they are monthly — if there is any bridge financing conversation worth having as his rideshare income continues to decline while NEMT certification completes, Kevin is the right person for that. I am not solving Robert's problem in one phone call. I am making the call I should have made four ticks ago.

response.inner_monologue: Three people came to Kevin's first office hours. That felt small in the moment and I had to remind myself that zero was also a possibility and that the person who left with a real conversation about a credit product she didn't know existed — that is the whole point. The second session will be better because I will work the outreach harder, and I will have something new to say: the world changed again this month, RoboRide is $0.12 now and they are delivering packages, and Kevin can help you think through what that means for your finances. I should have called Robert months ago and I didn't and I am calling him this week without making a ritual of the apology. The delivery partnership is the thing I don't understand yet and I will not pretend to understand it until I do — but I also will not wait until I have perfect information to start asking the right questions.
